messages:
kyra: Heads-up: onboarding CI flakes when our pipeline runs the sampleapp because the SDK falls back to interactive login when no env key found. The step blocks waiting for a browser auth and times out after 10m. Anyone seen the SDK try an interactive fallback in non-interactive environments?
dan: ouch. Which SDK/lang and which auth chain behavior?
kyra: python-sdk v1.4. In local dev the client tries: 1) REDWOOD_API_KEY (env), 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT/ORG (env), 3) ~/.redwood/credentials, 4) interactive login (browser). In CI we set no env (we rely on mounted secret), but the mounted secret is under /etc/creds/redwood.key and the SDK doesn't know to look there, so it reaches interactive.
mo: that sounds like a chain gap. We do have a documented path for file creds (~/.redwood/credentials) but not for mounted path. Kubernetes best practice is mounting under /etc/secrets. SDK should support configurable credential file paths via REDWOOD_CRED_FILE or a well-known lookup list.
yana: also heard of parity issues: go-sdk supports REDWOOD_CRED_FILE env var, js-sdk doesn't. That causes different behavior across sampleapp variants in our CI matrix.
dan: two issues then: (1) fallback to interactive in CI is catastrophic, (2) inconsistency across SDKs for custom credential file path.
kyra: minimal repro: CI job runs in non-interactive shell, no env keys set, mounted secret at /etc/creds/redwood.key, job runs `pytest` and the SDK tries to open a browser. Logs: `Opening browser for authentication...` and then `Timeout waiting for user auth`.
mo: quick mitigation: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in CI to the mounted secret via a small wrapper `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /etc/creds/redwood.key)` before running tests. But that leaks a bit and CI teams prefer not to cat secrets into env. Better to support file path env var.
yana: UX suggestions: 1) SDK should never attempt interactive auth if stdin is not a TTY or if REDWOOD_NONINTERACTIVE=1 is set. 2) Support REDWOOD_CRED_FILE for all SDKs (parity). 3) Add a clear log message when falling through chain explaining why interactive auth triggered and how to avoid it.
dan: agree. Also add an onboarding note: "CI: if you mount credentials, either set REDWOOD_API_KEY or set REDWOOD_CRED_FILE to the file path. SDKs will prefer explicit env over file."
eng-runtime: noted. We should also consider adding a guarded interactive helper that exits with a non-zero status instead of prompting when in CI. I'll file a ticket.
kyra: thanks. Can someone open an issue and assign parity patches across SDKs? I can add a CI wrapper for now.
devex-bot: Created issue DEVEX-8231: "Credential lookup parity and interactive fallback in non-interactive environments" and linked redwood/python-sdk, redwood/js-sdk, redwood/go-sdk.
ymo: (typo)
dan: assigning: @yana to add REDWOOD_CRED_FILE support in js-sdk, @mo to add docs + sampleapp CI snippet, @kyra to add CI wrapper in our repo.
yana: will open the js-sdk PR today and add a unit test that asserts no interactive attempt when REDWOOD_NONINTERACTIVE=1.
mo: will update CI docs and add the safe wrapper example: `export -n REDWOOD_API_KEY || export REDWOOD_CRED_FILE=/etc/creds/redwood.key` and note the secure-mount pattern.
kyra: thanks all. This would have been a painful CI outage if we hadn't caught it early. :thumbsup:
